'''Alfred Aeppli''' was a Swiss mathematician. The [[Pólya–Aeppli distribution]] in [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]] is named after him and his doctoral advisor [[George Pólya]].

== Life and work ==
Alfred Aeppli was born in [[Zürich]] on 15 July 1894 to Alfred Aeppli and Rosa Aeppli-Gehring. He went to a primary school in Zürich and the [[Canton of Zurich|canton]]'s Industrial School, where he received his [[matura]] in the summer of 1913. Afterwards, Aeppli studied at the [[ETH Zurich|Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule]] (ETH Zürich) at the department for higher teachers of mathematics and physics. In the winter semester of 1914–1915 he was on leave for military service. After receiving his [[Diplom]], he worked at a private school in Germany for a year and returned to the ETH in the spring of 1919 as a research assistant of [[Arthur Hirsch]].

Aeppli earned his doctorate in 1924 under the supervision of George Pólya and [[Hermann Weyl]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=30708|title=Alfred Aeppli}}</ref> He came up with the Pólya–Aeppli distribution in his doctoral dissertation.<ref>{{cite book|last=Aeppli |first=Alfred |title=Zur Theorie verketteter Wahrscheinlichkeiten: Markoff-Ketten höherer Ordnung |language=de |trans-title=On the theory of chained probabilities: Higher-order Markov chains |url=http://e-collection.library.ethz.ch/eserv/eth:20128/eth-20128-01.pdf |year=1924 |publisher=Gebr. Leemann & Co. A.-G. |location=Zurich}}</ref> This discovery was published by Pólya in 1930, and he credited its discovery to his student Aeppli.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Pólya |first=George |author-link=George Pólya |title=Sur quelques points de la théorie des probabilités |language=fr |trans-title=On some points of probability theory |url=http://archive.numdam.org/ARCHIVE/AIHP/AIHP_1930__1_2/AIHP_1930__1_2_117_0/AIHP_1930__1_2_117_0.pdf |volume=1 |issue=2 |journal=[[Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré]]|year=1930 |pages=117–161}}</ref> The Pólya–Aeppli distribution, now also known as the geometric Poisson distribution,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Sherbrooke |first=C. C. |year=1968 |title=Discrete compound Poisson processes and tables of the geometric Poisson distribution |journal=Naval Research Logistics Quarterly |volume=15 |pages=189–203}}</ref> is a particular case of the [[compound Poisson distribution]], and is used to describe objects that come in clusters, where the number of clusters follows a [[Poisson distribution]] and the number of objects within a cluster follows a [[geometric distribution]].<ref>{{cite book|first1=N.L. |last1=Johnson |first2=S. |last2=Kotz |first3=A.W. |last3=Kemp|author3-link=Adrienne W. Kemp |title=Univariate Discrete Distributions |publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons|Wiley]] |location=New York |date=2005 |edition=3rd}}</ref>
